name: an arrow at rest after a flat launch
source: recording sha256 c005ca31a2f5a47634f23f90d87d2b28a7ab6839b11e4266a0aaee8f83589564, vanilla 1.8.9 server sha256 c18e4245073aaff580eb7359902f0251436568b1647a9e443a924cdb73fa8312, 2026-08-18, entities summoned from the server console through the capture proxy
because: A landed projectile is compared at a looser bound than the wire's own, and this is the reason. The game stops an arrow where a ray cast hit and then backs it off along its own direction; this module sweeps a box and stops it against the floor, so the two disagree by up to one tick of the motion the arrow had left. Measured at 0.047 blocks on the 1.8.9 trajectory and 0.05 on the 26.1 ones, which is the backoff itself. The flight before the landing is compared at the wire's resolution; see the flight fixture beside this one.
